Concentric lunar electromagnetic launch system   

Purpose: A ground-based (lunar surface) electromagnetic accelerator/launcher for sending spacecraft from the Moon toward Earth orbit.    

Core Design: A large rotary arm (like a spinning catapult) fixed to a flat lunar surface via a central rotating shaft. A spacecraft is attached to one end of the arm.    

Propulsion Mechanism: Electromagnetic propulsion using a unilateral superconducting linear synchronous motor:    

Stator: Oblong coil windings arranged in concentric circular rings on the lunar surface.    

Mover: Superconducting magnet(s) on the rotary arm, excited by DC coils.  AC current in the stator creates a traveling magnetic wave; interaction with the mover's field generates propulsion force to spin the arm and accelerate the spacecraft to high velocity.    

Levitation/Stability: Electric suspension device (passive magnetic levitation):  Uses the same superconducting magnet to induce eddy currents in solid metal conductor plates (stators) arranged concentrically.    

Repulsive forces provide vertical suspension (to counter the arm's weight/gravity) and horizontal guiding (to balance centrifugal forces during rotation).    

No physical contact; fully magnetic/contactless  No direct prior art matches this exact concentric rotary + shared superconducting levitation combo for lunar application; it builds on known tech (superconducting motors, eddy-current maglev, rotary arms) but combines them in a novel way tailored to lunar ISRU (in-situ resource utilization) for returning materials (e.g., helium-3, regolith products) to Earth.
